title: Holloway Manufacturing - Infosec Questionnaire and Evidence Packet
content:
Executive summary:

This packet captures Redwood Inference's responses to Holloway Manufacturing's initial security and compliance questionnaire, the set of evidence artifacts collected for the POC, and notes from the technical workshop on 2025-02-25. The focus of the POC is secure hosting of inference for production telemetry processing (short text classification and structured output), meeting Holloway's requirement for EU data residency, and integration with their SIEM and KMS.

Scope and assumptions:
- Scope: Hosted API used for POC (dedicated pool option evaluated). No on-prem deployment in this phase.
- Data types: telemetry metadata, non-PII operational logs, and customer-supplied prompt sets (may contain PII for later phases; currently redacted).
- Residency: EU region (Frankfurt) will be used for POC traffic.
- Duration: 90-day POC, with canary traffic and simulated peak.

Questionnaire highlights (abbreviated Q&A):
Q: How is customer data isolated from other tenants?
A: Multi-tenant separation is provided by network and metadata isolation plus per-customer routing. For POC we recommend Dedicated GPU pools (reserved capacity) to achieve hardware isolation; if staying on hosted, request tenant-scoped model variants and enforced per-tenant KV cache namespaces. Relevant controls: per-tenant VPC egress and IAM roles, model-version pinning, and route-level quotas. Evidence: "dedicated-pool-config.yaml" and isolation diagram (artifact 1).

Q: Are logs and audit trails retained and accessible to customers?
A: Yes. Audit logs (control plane actions, model rollouts, API key usage) are shipped to the customer-configured logging endpoint during Private deployments. For hosted POC we provide export hooks to S3-compatible buckets and temporary SFTP. Log types, retention policies, and access control matrix are attached. Evidence: SIEM-integration-guide.pdf and example-audit-export-manifest.csv (artifact 3).

Q: How is encryption handled in transit and at rest?
A: TLS 1.2+ for all external endpoints; mutual TLS available for private peering. Data at rest is encrypted with AES-256. Customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS or HSM integration are supported for Private deployments and Dedicated encryption-at-rest for persisted model caches. Evidence: kms-integration-readme.md, hsm-control-matrix.xlsx (artifact 4).

Q: What authentication and identity controls exist?
A: API keys, OAuth2 SSO support (OIDC), and short-lived tokens for service-to-service calls. Role-based access control (RBAC) is enforced in the console and via IAM policies. SAML/SCIM provisioning examples included. Evidence: iam-policy-samples.json and sso-provisioning-playbook.docx (artifact 2).

Q: Do you perform vulnerability scanning and pen testing?
A: Yes. Quarterly external penetration tests are performed by a third-party. Internal vulnerability scans run weekly on the control plane and monthly on compute images. The latest pen test (Nov 2024) and remediation summary are attached. Evidence: pen-test-holloway-2024.pdf (artifact 6).

Evidence inventory (artifacts attached to this packet):
1) isolation-diagram-frankfurt.png - network/VPC and routing model for EU region (shows no cross-region egress for POC).
2) sso-provisioning-playbook.docx - SAML/SCIM setup steps and sample assertions for Holloway test tenant.
3) audit-export-manifest.csv - example exported audit log manifest for a 30-day window.
4) kms-integration-readme.md - walkthrough for attaching customer-managed KMS keys to Redwood Private and Dedicated deployments.
5) dedicated-pool-config.yaml - sample Dedicated pool configuration used in our throughput testing.
6) pen-test-holloway-2024.pdf - consolidated external pen test report redacted for public sections.
7) siem-integration-guide.pdf - instructions for forwarding control-plane and application events to Splunk/Elastic.
8) attestation-soc2-summary.pdf - SOC 2 Type II summary for Redwood control plane (latest audit period 2024).
9) cache-encryption-design.txt - description of KV cache encryption and key rotation plan.
10) data-residency-commitment-letter.pdf - brief agreement template that binds POC traffic to EU region for retention window.

Notes from technical workshop (2025-02-25):
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood), Ravi Patel (Redwood), Lena Ortiz (Redwood), Omar Haddad (Holloway), Priya Singh (Holloway), Julian Kramer (Holloway infra).
Agenda highlights and outcomes:
- Walked through end-to-end POC architecture (gateway -> regional router -> model serving). Holloway asked for explicit assurance that no non-EU control plane metadata would be persisted; we agreed to enable EU-only metadata routing for the POC and to deliver a short attestation (artifact 10).
- Discussed authentication: Holloway requested SAML SSO + SCIM for user provisioning and short-lived API tokens for automated ingestion. We provided an SSO playbook and will provide a SCIM connector test account.
- SIEM: Holloway uses Splunk; agreed to deliver sample enriched events for three event types (API_CALL, MODEL_DEPLOY, AUDIT_LOG) and validate ingestion during week 2.
- Performance: Baseline latency targets were set (p50 < 150ms for 512-token responses under dedicated pool). Redwood ran a micro-benchmark during the session and attached results (separate performance note).

Open items and risks:
- Data handling for PII in prompts: Holloway's test data included customer names in prompt examples. We recommended redaction for the POC and a later plan for data minimization and explicit consent if PII will be processed. Owner: Holloway compliance team.
- HSM-backed key escrow: Holloway prefers HSM keys for long-term run; Redwood can support HSM in Private mode but hosted API requires CMK via partner KMS. Action: Redwood infra to provide a cost/ops delta by 2025-03-10. Owner: Ravi Patel.
- SLA for dedicated capacity: Holloway asked for 99.95% latency SLOs under committed capacity. Sales/legal to draft a dedicated capacity amendment. Owner: Lena Ortiz.

Technical verification checklist (POC acceptance criteria):
- [ ] EU-only routing confirmed by network capture and attestation.
- [ ] Audit exports successfully delivered to Holloway Splunk test index.
- [ ] SSO + SCIM provisioning works end-to-end.
- [ ] Pen test remediation items status: high/critical items fixed or mitigated.
- [ ] CMK integration validated for encryption-at-rest on caches and S3 exports.

Remediation log (summary):
- Vulnerability CVE-2024-1123 (medium) patched on control plane 2024-12-15.
- Elevated permission discovered in legacy role fixed 2025-01-10; IAM policy tightened and attestation provided.

Regulatory notes relevant to Holloway (manufacturing supply chain):
- Data residency preference: EU only for PII and telemetry. Redwood currently supports region-bound storage for hosted and Private modes; Dedicated pools can be pinned to region-local hardware.
- Export controls: No restricted cryptography export to non-approved jurisdictions for customer-managed keys; neutral guidance attached.

Next steps and timeline:
- Week 1 (2025-03-02 to 2025-03-08): Enable EU-only metadata routing, provide attestation document, and create Holloway test tenant with SSO connector.
- Week 2: SIEM ingestion test and audit export validation.
- Week 3: Benchmark dedicated pool with Holloway workload; produce cost estimate for Dedicated and HSM option.
- Week 4: Review pen test remediation status and finalize POC acceptance criteria.

Sign-off (preliminary):
Prepared by: Maya Chen, Solutions Engineering
Technical reviewer: Ravi Patel, Infra
Legal reviewer: Lena Ortiz (pending dedicated amendment)

Document change log:
- 2025-02-18: Initial draft capturing questionnaire responses and initial evidence list.
- 2025-02-25: Workshop notes added and artifact list updated.
- 2025-03-05: Clarified KMS/HSM options and added remediation summary.

Notes to reviewers: This packet intentionally includes some redacted external artifacts for client confidentiality; full unredacted pen-test report and SOC artifacts will be shared under NDA. If you are reviewing on the Redwood network, follow linked_artifacts references to the secure evidence store for full documents.
